Prayer in both Petitions:

These Criminal Original Petitions are filed under Section 482  For Petitioners  in both Crl.O.Ps : Mr.A.Ramesh, Senior Counsel  for M/s.A.N.R.Jayaprathap  For Respondent : Mrs.M.F.Shabana, G.A. (Crl.Side)
 in both Crl.O.Ps COMMON ORDER

The petitioners have come forward with these two petitions seeking to quash the complaint in S.M.M.F.Nos.25 and 14 of 2011 respectively, on the file of the XX Metropolitan Magistrate Court,
Rippon Buildings Compound, Chennai 600 003.
2.According
to the petitioners, the 4th petitioner M/s.Sakthi Masala (P) Limited, engaged in the manufacture of high quality spice and curry powder etc., under the name and style SAKTHI.
The Officials, under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1994, collected samples on 11.02.2010 and sent for analysis.
Though the respondents have received the report on 12.03.2010 the complaint has been given only on 18.04.2011 and 06.07.2011.

3.According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, the entire packing is done with the supervision of the Quality Controller and they have been complying with the provisions under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1994.
It is further submitted that complaints have been erroneously given by the Officials, under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1994.
The complaints have been filed before the XX Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Rippon Buildings Compound, Chennai 600 003.

sentences.text: The complaint against the petitioners, for the offences said to have been committed under Section 7(ii) and 16(i)(a)(i) read with Section 2(ix)(k), 32(b)(2)(ii) and 32(b)(2)(v) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and Rule 32(b)(2)(ii) and (v) of the PFA Rules, 1955.

4.As per Section 11(4) of the Act, the respondents should have taken action within seven days on receipt of the report, but only after one year, the respondents have filed the complaints against the petitioners.

Taking note of the decision of this Court, in the case of Selvakumar vs. State reported in 2010 (2) FAC 304, this Court is inclined to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the Selvakumar vs The Food Inspector on 24 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53400203/

5.This Court by order in Crl.O.P.Nos.20273 and 22010 of 2009, dated 08.03.2016, in respect of V.Govindaraj and others v. The Food Inspector, Tiruppur Corporation, Tiruppur and V.Selvaraj and others v. The Food Inspector, Pollachi Municipality, Pollachi, has held as follows:

sentences.text: It is further submitted that complaints have been erroneously given by the Officials, under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The complaints have been filed before the Judicial Magistrate-I, Tirupur and the Judicial Magistrate-I, Pollachi.

The complaint against the petitioners, for the offences said to have been committed under Section 16(1)(a)(i) r/w 7(ii) & Section 2(ix)(K) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and Rule 36(7)(a) of the PFA Rules, 1955.

4.As per Section 11(4) of the Act, the respondents should have taken action within seven days on receipt of the report, but only after two years, the respondents have filed the complaints against the petitioners.

Taking note of the decision of this Court,
in the case of Selvakumar v. State reported in 2010 (2) FAC 304, this Court is inclined to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners and quash the proceedings only on the ground of laches.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If there are any further complaints, it is open to the respondents to proceed on merits, in accordance with law.
6.On fair reading of the above judgment rendered by this Court, it is made clear that the proceedings namely, the complaint filed belatedly after one year, as per Section 11(4) of the Act can be quashed on the ground of laches.

Therefore, this Court is inclined to accept the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, since the respondents, who is the complainants have received a report on 12.03.2010, but the complaint has been given only on 18.04.2011 and 06.07.2011, i.e.
beyond the limit of seven days as per Section 11(4) of the Act and both the complaints were quashed only on the ground of laches.
If there are any further complaints, it is open to the respondents to proceed on merits, in accordance with law.

7.In the result, both the Criminal Original Petitions are allowed and both the complaints in S.M.M.F.Nos.25 and 14 of 2011 respectively, on the file of the learned XX Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Rippon Buildings Compound, Chennai00 003, are quashed.
